# flightdeck_project (Resource)

Manages a Flightdeck project — the container for an application's work items, states, labels, members and integrations.

Creating a project seeds it the way the web form does (default workflow states, Task/Epic work item types, starter labels) and makes the token's user its admin. Deleting a project marks it for deletion and tears it down asynchronously; it disappears from the API immediately.

Updates carry the project's `lock_version` as an `If-Match` precondition. If the project was changed elsewhere since the last plan, the apply fails without overwriting anything; re-run `terraform plan`.

Every project this resource manages is marked `terraform_managed` unless its configuration says `terraform_managed = false`, which makes the settings Terraform owns read only in Flightdeck's web app. Setting that flag needs a workspace owner or admin token. Apply `terraform_managed = false` before removing a project from Terraform without destroying it, or it stays read only in the app.

A project can be imported by numeric id or by identifier: `terraform import flightdeck_project.app APP`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "flightdeck_project" "app" {
  name        = "Mobile App"
  identifier  = "APP"
  description = "The customer-facing mobile application"
  emoji       = "📱"
  network     = "private_project" # explicit members only; new projects are public

  # The deployed app this project belongs to (needs a workspace owner or admin
  # token). Optional: the first release event that names an app binds it.
  app = "mobile-app"

  # Only the feature keys listed here are managed; others keep their value.
  features = {
    intake = true
    errors = true
  }

  # terraform_managed defaults to true, which makes the settings Terraform owns
  # read only in Flightdeck's app (a change made there would be undone by the
  # next apply). Setting it needs a workspace owner or admin token.
}

# A project whose settings stay editable in Flightdeck's app. Before removing a
# project from Terraform without destroying it (a `removed` block or
# `terraform state rm`), apply terraform_managed = false like this, or it stays
# read only in the app.
resource "flightdeck_project" "sandbox" {
  name              = "Sandbox"
  identifier        = "SBX"
  terraform_managed = false
}

# Self-healing (workspace admins only). `rollback` is the loop's mode:
# "report" notes what it would do and never touches production, and "auto"
# lets Flightdeck roll production back by itself when every check passes.
resource "flightdeck_project" "payments" {
  name       = "Payments"
  identifier = "PAY"

  self_healing = {
    feature_enabled        = true
    rollback               = "report"
    bake_minutes           = 30
    burn_rate              = 10.0
    max_rollbacks_per_hour = 2
  }
}

# Auto-promote (workspace owners and admins only) lets Flightdeck promote a
# project's release candidates to production by itself once every check
# passes. It needs auto-rollback as its safety net, and it goes to Flightdeck
# in the same request as self_healing. Each window part you set replaces only
# that part.
resource "flightdeck_project" "storefront" {
  name       = "Storefront"
  identifier = "STORE"

  self_healing = {
    feature_enabled = true
    rollback        = "auto"
  }

  auto_promote = {
    mode           = "deps_only" # only when every waiting change is a Dependabot update
    soak_hours     = 24
    heads_up_hours = 4
    window = {
      days      = ["mon", "tue", "wed", "thu"]
      start     = "09:00"
      end       = "15:00"
      time_zone = "America/Chicago"
    }
    freeze_dates = ["2030-12-24", "2030-12-31"] # [] clears the list
  }
}

# A project's Slack channel (project admins). Provisioning is asynchronous:
# enabling the channel enqueues the job, and `channel_id` and
# `provision_status` are filled in once it has run.
resource "flightdeck_project" "support" {
  name       = "Support"
  identifier = "SUP"

  slack_channel = {
    enabled = true
    name    = "team-support" # omit to use the project-name default

    # "link" uses a channel that already exists and never invites anyone.
    # For a private channel, invite the Flightdeck app to it in Slack first.
    # "create" makes a new channel and invites the project's members. Leave
    # it out to keep whatever the project already has.
    mode = "link"

    # Only the categories listed here are managed; the API merges them, so
    # removing one leaves it as it is rather than restoring its default.
    event_filter = {
      logged        = true
      field_changed = false
    }
  }
}

# Agent work (workspace owners and admins only) lets AutoPilot agents take the
# work items a person marks with the agent label, and open pull requests for
# them. A flightdeck_label in the project depends on the project, so pointing
# label_id at one would be a dependency cycle; for a project that already
# exists, the label takes its project_id from a data source instead.
data "flightdeck_project" "billing" {
  identifier = "BILL"
}

resource "flightdeck_label" "agent_ready" {
  project_id = data.flightdeck_project.billing.id
  name       = "agent-ready"
}

# A second label sends an item to an agent for research first, rather than to
# be built. It must be a different label from the agent label, and it only
# sends work while research is one of the project's kinds.
resource "flightdeck_label" "research_first" {
  project_id = data.flightdeck_project.billing.id
  name       = "research-first"
}

# The service account agents work as. It needs a project role that can edit
# work items, because a claimed item is assigned to it.
data "flightdeck_workspace_member" "agent" {
  email = "agent-bot@example.com"
}

resource "flightdeck_project_member" "agent" {
  project_id = data.flightdeck_project.billing.id
  user_id    = data.flightdeck_workspace_member.agent.id
  role       = "member"
}

resource "flightdeck_project" "billing" {
  name       = "Billing"
  identifier = "BILL"

  agent_work = {
    enabled = true
    # Add a kind only once AutoPilot allows it for the project.
    kinds             = ["implement-work-item", "fix-error", "research"]
    label_id          = flightdeck_label.agent_ready.id
    research_label_id = flightdeck_label.research_first.id
    agent_account_id  = data.flightdeck_workspace_member.agent.id
    max_in_progress   = 1
    daily_budget_usd  = 10
    task_max_usd      = 2.5 # whole cents: more decimal places fail the plan
    # Ask AutoPilot to turn on GitHub auto-merge for the agents' pull
    # requests. AutoPilot's app and the repository must allow it too, and
    # GitHub merges only once the required checks and reviews pass.
    auto_merge = true
    # Send items Flightdeck files for failed CI runs to an agent without
    # waiting for a person to add the agent label. Only workflows on the
    # GitHub integration's ci_workflows list count.
    send_ci_failures = true
    # Send items Flightdeck's error alert rules file to an agent as
    # fix-error, without waiting for a person to add the agent label. It
    # needs "fix-error" in kinds, and only items filed after it is turned on
    # count.
    send_errors = true
    # Don't have agents wait for CI (on by default): for a repository whose
    # CI takes longer than an agent should wait. The agent finishes once it
    # has pushed, and Flightdeck re-runs or follows up on a failed run itself
    # for workflows on the GitHub integration's ci_workflows list.
    wait_for_checks = false
    # The AI model each kind of work runs on. A kind left out uses
    # AutoPilot's default. Flightdeck names the models it offers, and
    # refuses one it doesn't. Opus spends the budget faster than Sonnet.
    models = {
      "implement-work-item" = "opus-5-5"
      "research"            = "sonnet-5-5"
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `identifier` (String) Short key that prefixes work item keys (`APP-123`). 1–10 uppercase letters or digits, starting with a letter; unique within the workspace.
- `name` (String) Display name.

### Optional

- `agent_work` (Attributes) Agent work settings, managed through the project's `agent-work` API resource: whether AutoPilot, the AI agents Flightdeck sends work to, may take this project's work items, which labels mark an item for them, which AI model each kind of work runs on, whether items filed for failed CI runs or logged errors go to them without a label, the service account they work as, whether they wait for CI on their pull requests, and how much they may spend and run. An agent works on a copy of the project's GitHub repository and opens a pull request, which a person reviews and merges unless `auto_merge` is on. Reading and writing these settings requires the token's user to be a **workspace owner or admin**; for other tokens, and on a Flightdeck version without the endpoint, the block is null.

Agent work is off until `enabled` turns it on. A plan that turns it on carries a warning saying so, and while it is on, each thing that stops Flightdeck sending work right now (the API's `blockers`: no agent label or research label chosen, no linked GitHub repository, the day's budget spent, and so on) is shown as a warning on refresh and after apply rather than stored, because it changes as the project does.

The endpoint merges, so this block only ever sends what you configure, and a setting you never name keeps whatever the project has, including a value changed on the settings page. `label_id` and `agent_account_id` are never sent unless configured, because the API reads an empty value for either as "clear it"; removing one from configuration therefore leaves the stored choice in place (clear it on the project's **Agent work** settings page). `research_label_id` works the same way.

These settings have their own `lock_version`, separate from the project's: a write here never conflicts with a project update and does not bump the project's `lock_version`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--agent_work))
- `app` (String) The deployed app this project belongs to, as the deploy pipeline's release events name it: the app's GitHub repository name, 1 to 100 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`. One project is one app, and within a workspace an app belongs to at most one project (compared ignoring case), so an app another project already has fails the apply (`app_taken`). Setting or changing it needs a **workspace owner or admin** token, even where the token could otherwise update the project. When unset, the project's current app is kept: the first release event that names an app binds the project to it, so leaving this unset leaves the binding to the pipeline. The API can set or change `app` but never clear it (a workspace admin can, in Flightdeck's project settings), so removing it from configuration does not unbind the project. That first binding bumps the project's `lock_version`, so an apply racing it fails once with a lock conflict; run `terraform plan` again and re-apply.
- `archived` (Boolean) Whether the project is archived. New projects are not archived. When unset, the project's current value is kept (so importing an archived project does not unarchive it).
- `auto_promote` (Attributes) Auto-promote settings: whether Flightdeck promotes this project's release candidates to production by itself, and when it may. They are written through the project's `self-healing` API resource, beside `self_healing.rollback`, because auto-rollback is auto-promote's safety net, so reading and writing them requires the token's user to be a **workspace owner or admin**; for other tokens the attribute is null. When an apply changes both `self_healing` and `auto_promote`, they go to Flightdeck in one request, which Flightdeck checks whole before it saves anything.

Auto-promote is off until `mode` turns it on. A plan that turns it on carries a warning saying so. While it is on, each thing that stops Flightdeck promoting right now (the API's `auto_promote_blockers`, such as auto-rollback not being on, or anything that would stop auto-rollback) is shown as a warning on refresh and after apply rather than stored, because it changes as the project does. A Flightdeck that can't promote yet lists `not_yet_available` for every project; the settings are saved there and take effect once promoting ships.

The endpoint merges, so this attribute only ever sends what you configure, including each part of `window` on its own, and a setting you never name keeps whatever the project has. Each one you leave unset follows Flightdeck's default until someone sets it. A write here bumps the project's `lock_version`.

Needs a Flightdeck that supports auto-promote. On an older one the attribute reads as null, and setting anything in it fails with an error that asks you to upgrade Flightdeck. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auto_promote))
- `description` (String) Free-text description. Removing it from configuration clears it.
- `emoji` (String) Emoji shown next to the project name. Defaults to the server's default (📁).
- `features` (Map of Boolean) Feature toggles to manage, as a map of feature key to boolean. Only the keys listed here are managed; keys you leave out keep whatever value the project has. Settable keys: `cycles`, `epics`, `milestones`, `views`, `pages`, `meeting_notes`, `decisions`, `intake`, `errors`, `incidents`, `estimates`. `modules` is the old name of `epics`: it still works, with a deprecation warning, and is sent as `epics`; rename it. `self_healing` and `slack` are reported by the `flightdeck_project` data source and refused here, because each is settable on its own endpoint: self-healing through the `self_healing` block, and `slack` — the Slack notifications master switch — as `slack_channel.notifications_enabled`.
- `github_repo_full_name` (String) GitHub repository this project is linked to, as `owner/repo`. **Read-only**: the API refuses writes to this field. Manage the link with a `flightdeck_github_integration` resource, which sets it on link and clears it on unlink.
- `lead_id` (Number) User id of the project lead, which a `flightdeck_workspace_member` data source resolves from an email address. A new lead must be a member of the workspace and not a guest; Flightdeck checks the role, so naming a guest fails the apply rather than the plan. The lead the project already has is always accepted back: a guest who was named before Flightdeck refused guests or was made a guest since, and someone who has left the workspace. Defaults to the token's user on create. When unset, the current lead is kept.
- `network` (String) Project visibility: `public_project` (every workspace member can see it) or `private_project` (explicit members only). New projects are public. When unset, the current value is kept. Making a project private also gives the token's user and the project lead admin memberships so nobody is locked out (the lead only while they are a workspace member and not a guest); members who lose implicit access are not notified.
- `self_healing` (Attributes) Self-healing (automated rollback) control-loop configuration, managed through the project's `self-healing` API resource. Reading and writing it requires the token's user to be a **workspace admin**; for other tokens, and on a Flightdeck version without the endpoint, the block is null.

Two settings decide whether the loop acts, and both are settable here. `feature_enabled` puts the project in front of the loop at all. `rollback` is its mode: `"report"` (**report only**: it notes what it would do and never touches production) or `"auto"` (**auto-rollback**: it rolls production back by itself when every check passes, and pages a person when it can't). The loop acts only when `feature_enabled` is on, `rollback` is `"auto"`, and Flightdeck's global kill switch is off. A plan that turns auto-rollback on carries a warning saying so, and while `rollback` is `"auto"` each thing that would stop it right now is shown as a warning on refresh and after apply. `armed` is the old name for the mode, kept read-only and deprecated.

The endpoint merges, so this block only ever sends what you configure: a threshold you leave unset keeps whatever the project has (the server's documented default, until someone overrides it), and a setting you never name is never disturbed — including one changed in the console. `short_window_minutes` must not exceed `long_window_minutes`, and the API checks that against the merged result — so a write naming only one of them can still be refused by the other's stored value. Setting both incoherently fails the plan; raising one past a stored value the configuration does not mention is a plan-time **warning**, since the stored value is only as current as the last refresh. A write here bumps the project's `lock_version`. The `self_healing` key is refused in `features`; it is spelled `feature_enabled` here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--self_healing))
- `slack_channel` (Attributes) Per-project Slack channel configuration, managed through the project's `slack-channel` API resource. Reading and writing it requires the token's user to be an **admin of this project** (a workspace owner or admin qualifies); for other tokens, and on a Flightdeck version without the endpoint, the block is null.

**Provisioning is asynchronous, after one synchronous check.** When a write leaves the channel enabled and not yet linked, Flightdeck first looks the channel up in Slack. If it exists but Flightdeck cannot post to it (a private channel the Flightdeck bot is not a member of, or an archived channel), the API answers HTTP 422 (`slack_channel_unusable`) and saves nothing. On an update the apply fails with Flightdeck's message, which names the channel and the bot to invite, and the next plan still shows the change: invite the bot, or choose a different `name`, and apply again. On the apply that creates the project, the provider gives the same message as a warning instead, so the new project is kept as created; the next plan shows the Slack change again, and the next apply retries the channel. A channel that does not exist yet passes the check, since Flightdeck can create it, unless `mode` is `link`. The same 422 refuses a channel that `mode` rules out, as described there. If Slack is rate limiting or unavailable, the check is skipped and the write goes ahead.

Once the check passes, Flightdeck saves the configuration and enqueues a job that creates the channel if needed, links it and invites the project's members (in `link` mode it invites nobody). The write may come back already `linked`, but usually `channel_id`, `linked`, `provision_status` and `provision_note` are filled in afterwards and a later refresh picks them up. An apply that ends with `provision_status` at `queued` has succeeded: it does not wait for Slack, and the pending values never produce a diff. If the write comes back with `provision_status` at `failed`, or at `needs_invite` (linked, but Flightdeck is not in the channel and cannot join it, so it cannot invite anyone), the provider warns and passes `provision_note` along rather than failing, since the configuration is saved.

Nothing provisions at all when `available` is false (the workspace has no connected Slack integration) or `scopes_sufficient` is false (the connection predates the channel scopes). Both are fixed by re-authorizing Slack under Settings → Integrations, which the API cannot do; the provider warns rather than failing, since the configuration is still stored.

A write here bumps the project's `lock_version`. Attributes map onto the API's keys by dropping the `slack_` prefix (`enabled` is `slack_channel_enabled`, `mode` is `slack_channel_mode`, `notifications_enabled` is `slack_notifications_enabled`, `name` is `slack_channel_name`, `event_filter` is `slack_event_filter`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--slack_channel))
- `terraform_managed` (Boolean) Whether Terraform manages this project's settings. While it is `true`, Flightdeck's web app makes the settings Terraform owns read only (name, identifier, description, emoji, lead, visibility, deployed app, feature toggles, the Slack channel, and the agent work and auto-promote settings) and turns off archiving and restoring the project, and Flightdeck's MCP tools refuse to change them, because a change made by hand would be undone by the next apply. Flightdeck's API, which this provider uses, still writes everything. Members, states, labels and the rest stay editable in the app. Defaults to `true`; set it to `false` to leave the project editable in the app.

Setting or changing it needs a token whose user is a **workspace owner or admin**, on a create too. Sending the value Flightdeck already has is fine for any token, so a token that is not an owner or admin can still update a project whose flag already matches the configuration. Such a token can create a project only with `terraform_managed = false`. To leave an existing project's flag as it is, add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [terraform_managed] }` to it.

Removing a project from Terraform without destroying it (a `removed` block, or `terraform state rm`) leaves the flag on, so the project stays read only in the app. To hand a project back to the app, apply `terraform_managed = false` first, then remove it from Terraform.

Importing a project that is not marked yet plans an update that sets it to `true`.

Needs a Flightdeck that supports `terraform_managed`. Against an older one, a project that already exists keeps working while this is unset: it reads as null and the provider does not send it. Creating a project (even with `terraform_managed = false`, since a create always sends it), or setting this explicitly, fails there with an error asking you to upgrade Flightdeck. The `flightdeck_project` data source tells the two apart: its `terraform_managed` is null on a Flightdeck without the setting.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) Numeric id of the project.
- `lock_version` (Number) Optimistic-locking version the API bumps on every change (including self-healing and Slack channel writes, and the deploy pipeline binding the project's `app`). Sent as `If-Match` on updates. Agent work settings have their own, `agent_work.lock_version`.

<a id="nestedatt--agent_work"></a>
### Nested Schema for `agent_work`

Optional:

- `accept_machine_labels` (Boolean) Whether the agent label and the research label count even when a machine added them (an automation rule, an import, a service account). Off by default, so only a label a person adds sends an item to an agent. When unset, the project's current value is kept.
- `agent_account_id` (Number) User id of the workspace **service account** agents work as: a claimed item is assigned to it while an agent works on it, so it also needs a project role that can edit work items (a `flightdeck_project_member`). A `flightdeck_workspace_member` data source resolves one from its email address (service accounts are visible to workspace admins, and its `kind` is `service`); the id is also on the workspace's **Service accounts** settings page. When unset, the stored account is kept; it is never sent empty, because the API would read that as clearing it.
- `auto_merge` (Boolean) Whether to ask AutoPilot to turn on GitHub auto-merge for each pull request an agent opens for this project. Off by default. AutoPilot's app for the repository, and the repository's own settings and ruleset, must allow auto-merge too; if any of them doesn't, the pull request waits for a person. GitHub merges only once the required checks and reviews pass. Flightdeck never merges anything itself. When unset, the project's current value is kept; set it explicitly, even to `false`, for Terraform to own it.

Needs a Flightdeck that supports `auto_merge`. On an older one it reads as null and is never sent while it is unset. Setting it there fails an update with an error that asks you to upgrade Flightdeck. On the apply that creates the project it is a warning instead, so the new project isn't marked tainted, and the next plan shows what is still to apply.
- `base_ref` (String) The branch agents start from. Default `main`. Must be a branch name Git allows. When unset, the project's current value is kept.
- `daily_budget_usd` (Number) The most agent work may cost this project in one UTC day, in US dollars (default 10). More than 0 and at most 1000, with **at most two decimal places**: Flightdeck refuses more rather than rounding, so the plan does too. When unset, the project's current value is kept.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether AutoPilot agents may take this project's work items. Off by default. Once it is on and nothing in `blockers` stands in the way, agents take each work item a person marks with the agent label (and, while `send_ci_failures` is on, each item Flightdeck files for a failed CI run, and while `send_errors` is on, each item an error alert rule files) and open pull requests for it, and, while `research` is one of the kinds, research each item marked with the research label and post a report on it. A plan that turns it on warns. Flightdeck posts the change to the project's Slack updates. When unset, the project's current value is kept; set it explicitly, even to `false`, for Terraform to own it.
- `kinds` (Set of String) The kinds of work agents may do. Known kinds: `implement-work-item`, `fix-error`, `research`. None by default, and an empty set clears the list. Add `fix-error` or `research` only once AutoPilot allows that kind for the project: if AutoPilot refuses a kind, it holds all of the project's agent work, other kinds included. When unset, the project's current list is kept.
- `label_id` (Number) Id of the label in this project that marks a work item for an agent. Only a label a person adds after it is chosen here counts (see `label_chosen_at`), unless `accept_machine_labels` says otherwise. When unset, the stored label is kept; it is never sent empty, because the API would read that as clearing it.

A `flightdeck_label` in this project depends on the project, so referring to it here forms a dependency cycle. For a project that already exists, give the label its `project_id` from a `flightdeck_project` **data source** looked up by `identifier`, which breaks the cycle; otherwise create the label first and set the id afterwards.
- `max_in_progress` (Number) How many items agents may work on at once (default 1). A whole number from 1 to 10. When unset, the project's current value is kept.
- `models` (Map of String) Which AI model each kind of work runs on, as a map from kind of work to model name, for example `{ "implement-work-item" = "opus-5-5" }`. The keys are kinds of work: `implement-work-item`, `fix-error` and `research`, and the plan fails on any other key. Each kind needs a model name; a blank one fails the plan. A kind left out of the map uses AutoPilot's default (Sonnet 5.5 today), and `{}` puts every kind back on the default. Setting it replaces the whole map Flightdeck holds, so a kind removed from it goes back to the default.

Flightdeck names the models it offers (`sonnet-5-5` and `opus-5-5` today, and the list may grow), so the provider doesn't check model names: Flightdeck refuses a model it doesn't offer, and the apply fails with its message, which lists the ones it does. A model Flightdeck no longer offers is still accepted for the kind it is already set for, so a configuration that names it keeps applying. A work item's own agent model, set in Flightdeck, wins over this. Opus costs more than Sonnet, so the daily budget and each task's limit run out sooner. If AutoPilot doesn't run a model named here, it refuses the tasks that ask for it, and Flightdeck holds the project's agent work for a while (the `model_refused` blocker). When unset, the project's current models are kept; set it explicitly, even to `{}`, for Terraform to own it.

Needs a Flightdeck that supports `models`. On an older one it reads as null and is never sent while it is unset. Setting it there fails an update with an error that asks you to upgrade Flightdeck. On the apply that creates the project it is a warning instead, so the new project isn't marked tainted, and the next plan shows what is still to apply.
- `queue_minutes` (Number) How many minutes a task may wait to start before it is dropped (default 60). A whole number from 1 to 1440. When unset, the project's current value is kept.
- `research_label_id` (Number) Id of the label in this project that sends a work item to an agent for **research** first, rather than to be built: the agent looks into it and posts a report on the item as a comment. It must be a different label from `label_id`. The plan fails when the configuration sets both to the same id, and Flightdeck refuses it when one of them matches the other's stored value. Like the agent label, only a label a person adds after it is chosen here counts (see `research_label_chosen_at`), unless `accept_machine_labels` says otherwise. Flightdeck sends an item as research only while `research` is in the project's kinds of work. When unset, the stored label is kept; it is never sent empty, because the API would read that as clearing it.

Needs the Flightdeck release that added the agent work research label. A label in this project forms the same dependency cycle as `label_id`, and the same data source breaks it.
- `runbook` (String) The steps the agent follows for `implement-work-item`. Known runbooks: `implement-work-item@1` (the default). `fix-error` and `research` always use their own runbook. When unset, the project's current value is kept.
- `send_ci_failures` (Boolean) Whether to send each work item Flightdeck files for a failed CI run to an agent without waiting for a person to add the agent label. Off by default, so such an item waits for a person to label it. It applies only to items filed for workflows on the linked repository's CI workflows list (`ci_workflows` on `flightdeck_github_integration`), and only while the integration files CI failures (`ci_failure_action` isn't `off`), an agent label is chosen (`label_id`) and `implement-work-item` is one of the `kinds`; an item that waits in intake goes once someone accepts it. Flightdeck sends each such item once: after an agent has worked on it, it goes again only when a person adds the agent label. At most one item per workflow (per job, for a flaky test) goes this way in 24 hours, and never one a person is assigned to. The usual limits still hold, such as `max_in_progress` and the budget. Turning it on or off is posted to the project's Slack updates. When unset, the project's current value is kept; set it explicitly, even to `false`, for Terraform to own it.

Needs a Flightdeck that supports `send_ci_failures`. On an older one it reads as null and is never sent while it is unset. Setting it there fails an update with an error that asks you to upgrade Flightdeck. On the apply that creates the project it is a warning instead, so the new project isn't marked tainted, and the next plan shows what is still to apply.
- `send_errors` (Boolean) Whether to send each work item one of Flightdeck's error alert rules files to an agent, as `fix-error`, without waiting for a person to add the agent label. Off by default, so such an item waits for a person to label it. It applies only while `fix-error` is one of the `kinds` and an agent label is chosen (`label_id`), and only to items filed since it was last turned on, within the last 24 hours: turning it on never sends the items already in the backlog. The error must be at `error` or `critical` level and still active (not muted, snoozed or resolved), and the alert rule that filed the item must still be on and still file work items. Flightdeck waits 15 minutes after an item is filed (or accepted, for an item that waits in intake), so a person who sees the alert can take it first, and never sends one a person is assigned to or has started. It sends each such item once, and only one item per error: after that, an item goes again only when a person adds the agent label. The usual limits still hold, such as `max_in_progress` and the budget. Turning it on or off is posted to the project's Slack updates. When unset, the project's current value is kept; set it explicitly, even to `false`, for Terraform to own it.

Needs a Flightdeck that supports `send_errors`. On an older one it reads as null and is never sent while it is unset. Setting it there fails an update with an error that asks you to upgrade Flightdeck. On the apply that creates the project it is a warning instead, so the new project isn't marked tainted, and the next plan shows what is still to apply.
- `task_max_minutes` (Number) The most minutes one task may run (default 30). A whole number from 1 to 240. When unset, the project's current value is kept.
- `task_max_usd` (Number) The most one task may cost, in US dollars (default 5). It may not exceed `daily_budget_usd`, which Flightdeck checks against the stored budget when only one of the two is set. More than 0 and at most 100, with **at most two decimal places**: Flightdeck refuses more rather than rounding, so the plan does too. When unset, the project's current value is kept.
- `wait_for_checks` (Boolean) Whether an agent waits for its pull request's CI checks, and fixes a failure itself, before it finishes. **On by default**, unlike the other switches here. Set it to `false` for a repository whose CI takes longer than an agent should wait: AutoPilot is then asked not to wait for CI on each pull request task, so the agent finishes once it has pushed, and Flightdeck deals with a failed run itself: it re-runs the failed jobs once and, if they fail again, sends the item back to an agent to fix. Flightdeck does that only for workflows on the linked repository's CI workflows list (`ci_workflows` on `flightdeck_github_integration`), so with this off, a failure in a workflow that isn't on the list is left for a person. It never stops agent work from starting. When unset, the project's current value is kept; set it explicitly, even to `true`, for Terraform to own it.

Needs a Flightdeck that supports `wait_for_checks`. On an older one it reads as null and is never sent while it is unset. Setting it there fails an update with an error that asks you to upgrade Flightdeck. On the apply that creates the project it is a warning instead, so the new project isn't marked tainted, and the next plan shows what is still to apply.

Read-Only:

- `label_chosen_at` (String) When `label_id` was last set to a label (RFC 3339), or null while none is chosen. Only a label a person adds after this time counts, so renaming an old label to the agent label brings none of its items along. Read-only: Flightdeck sets it whenever `label_id` changes.
- `lock_version` (Number) Optimistic-locking version of these settings, separate from the project's. 0 while the project's settings were never saved. Sent as `If-Match` on every write here.
- `research_label_chosen_at` (String) When `research_label_id` was last set to a label (RFC 3339), or null while none is chosen. Only a label a person adds after this time counts. Read-only: Flightdeck sets it whenever `research_label_id` changes.


<a id="nestedatt--auto_promote"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auto_promote`

Optional:

- `freeze_dates` (Set of String) Days Flightdeck never promotes on, as ISO dates such as `"2026-12-24"`, at most 100. A date that has passed stays until you remove it, so it never shows as drift. `[]` clears the list. When unset, the project's current dates are kept.
- `heads_up_hours` (Number) How long before a promote Flightdeck posts a heads-up in the project's Slack channel, so someone can hold it, in hours (default 4). A whole number from 1 to 72. When unset, the project's current value is kept.
- `mode` (String) Whether Flightdeck promotes release candidates by itself: `"off"` (the default) never does, `"deps_only"` promotes only when every change waiting for production is a Dependabot update, and `"all"` promotes any release candidate that passes every check. A plan that moves it away from `"off"` carries a warning. A blocked mode is still accepted: the blockers are shown as warnings instead. Flightdeck posts each change of mode to Slack (the project's channel, or the workspace's for a project that isn't private). When unset, the project's current mode is kept, so removing `mode`, or the whole `auto_promote` block, does not turn auto-promote off: set it to `"off"`. A plan that leaves it unset while it is on warns that it stays on.
- `soak_hours` (Number) How long a release candidate must run on stage before it may be promoted, in hours (default 24). A whole number from 4 to 720. When unset, the project's current value is kept.
- `window` (Attributes) When a promote may start. The default is Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 16:00, `America/New_York`. Each part is sent only when configured, and Flightdeck merges it into the window the project has, then checks the window as a whole, so setting only `start` can still be refused for the `end` the project already has. A plan that sets both checks that `start` comes first. One that sets only one checks it against the other: on a new project that is Flightdeck's default window, and a window that would not fit fails the plan; on an existing project it is the value stored at the last refresh, and a mismatch is a warning. When unset, the project's current window is kept. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auto_promote--window))

<a id="nestedatt--auto_promote--window"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auto_promote.window`

Optional:

- `days` (Set of String) The days of the week a promote may start on: at least one of `mon`, `tue`, `wed`, `thu`, `fri`, `sat`, `sun`. When unset, the current days are kept.
- `end` (String) When the window closes each day, as 24-hour `HH:MM` with two-digit hours, up to `24:00`, which is the end of the day. It must come after `start`. When unset, the current end is kept.
- `start` (String) When the window opens each day, as 24-hour `HH:MM` with two-digit hours, from `00:00` to `23:59`. It must come before `end`, since a window can't run past midnight. When unset, the current start is kept.
- `time_zone` (String) The time zone `start` and `end` are in, as an IANA name spelled exactly, such as `America/New_York` (not `Eastern Time (US & Canada)`). Flightdeck checks the name. When unset, the current time zone is kept.



<a id="nestedatt--self_healing"></a>
### Nested Schema for `self_healing`

Optional:

- `absolute_floor` (Number) …and at least this many errors per minute, guarding a near-zero baseline (default 5.0). Must be greater than 0 and at most 100000; the API refuses non-positive values because the engine treats them as "no limit".
- `bake_minutes` (Number) Eligibility window after a deploy, in minutes (default 20). Must be between 1 and 1440; the API refuses non-positive values because the engine treats them as "no limit".
- `baseline_multiplier` (Number) Post-deploy error rate must be at least this multiple of the baseline (default 5.0). Must be greater than 0 and at most 1000; the API refuses non-positive values because the engine treats them as "no limit".
- `burn_rate` (Number) Multi-window burn rate that counts as severe (default 14.4). Must be greater than 0 and at most 1000; the API refuses non-positive values because the engine treats them as "no limit".
- `consecutive_error_limit` (Number) Metrics-query failures tolerated before a decision is inconclusive (default 3). Must be between 1 and 100; the API refuses non-positive values because the engine treats them as "no limit".
- `cooldown_minutes` (Number) No action on the same app within this window, in minutes (default 30). Must be between 1 and 1440; the API refuses non-positive values because the engine treats them as "no limit".
- `count_browser_errors` (Boolean) Whether errors sent with a browser token count toward the error rate the loop acts on, and toward the baseline a release is compared against. The server's default is `false`, so only errors sent with a server token count: a browser token ships inside every page, so anyone can read it and post fake errors to push the rate over the trigger. Either way, browser errors still show on the Errors pages and fire any error alert rule that counts them (see `flightdeck_error_alert_rule`'s `condition.count_browser_errors`). When unset, the project's current value is kept. Null on a Flightdeck that predates the setting, where a configured value fails the apply.
- `feature_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the self-healing control loop runs for this project at all. With `rollback` at `"report"` (report only), turning this on starts the observation, not the automation: the loop notes what it would do and never touches production, although it can still notify people and file work. With `rollback` at `"auto"`, turning this on is going live, and Flightdeck refuses it unless the same apply sets `rollback`, so a project stored as auto-rollback needs `rollback` in configuration before this can turn it on. Setting this to `false` pauses the loop and leaves `rollback` where it is. When unset, the project's current value is kept, so a switch flipped in the console survives an apply; set it explicitly, even to `false`, for Terraform to own it.
- `long_window_minutes` (Number) Long burn-rate window in minutes (default 60). Must be between 1 and 1440; the API refuses non-positive values because the engine treats them as "no limit".
- `max_rollbacks_per_hour` (Number) Per-app blast-radius cap (default 1). Must be between 1 and 100; the API refuses non-positive values because the engine treats them as "no limit".
- `recovery_window_minutes` (Number) Grace period after a rollback before a still-severe signal escalates, in minutes (default 15). Must be between 1 and 1440; the API refuses non-positive values because the engine treats them as "no limit".
- `rollback` (String) The loop's mode: `"report"` for **report only**, where it notes what it would do and never touches production, or `"auto"` for **auto-rollback**, where Flightdeck rolls production back by itself when every check passes and pages a person when it can't. It acts only while `feature_enabled` is on. A plan that moves this to `"auto"` carries a warning saying so. While it is `"auto"`, each thing that would stop auto-rollback right now (the API's `rollback_blockers`, such as a release that is not marked safe to roll back) is shown as a warning on refresh and after apply rather than stored, because it changes with every deploy. `"auto"` is accepted even while something blocks it. When unset, the project's current mode is kept, so a mode changed in the console survives an apply; set it explicitly for Terraform to own it. Needs a Flightdeck that supports the setting; an older one reports the mode through `armed` only, and a configured value fails the apply.
- `short_window_minutes` (Number) Short burn-rate window in minutes (default 5). Must be between 1 and 1440; the API refuses non-positive values because the engine treats them as "no limit".
- `sustain_count` (Number) Consecutive trips required before acting (default 3). Must be between 1 and 100; the API refuses non-positive values because the engine treats them as "no limit".

Read-Only:

- `armed` (Boolean, Deprecated) Whether auto-rollback is on: the API's `armed` flag, true exactly when `rollback` is `"auto"`. Read-only. Deprecated: read and set `rollback` instead.


<a id="nestedatt--slack_channel"></a>
### Nested Schema for `slack_channel`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether this project gets its own Slack channel. When unset, the project's current value is kept. Turning it on enqueues provisioning once Flightdeck has checked that it can post to the channel (see above); turning it off stops future posts but never deletes the channel on Slack.
- `event_filter` (Map of Boolean) Activity categories to post, as a map of category to boolean. Categories: `created`, `state_changed`, `field_changed`, `logged`, `assigned` (defaults: `created`, `state_changed` and `assigned` on, `field_changed` and `logged` off). The API MERGES this map rather than replacing it, so it declares overrides: only the categories listed here are managed, and removing one leaves it at its current value rather than restoring its default — set it explicitly to change it back.
- `mode` (String) How Flightdeck gets the channel: `create` or `link`. With `create`, Flightdeck creates the channel and invites the project's members, when it sets the channel up and again whenever someone joins the project; if another channel already has the name, the write is refused. With `link`, Flightdeck uses a channel that already exists, joining it if it is public, and **never invites anyone**: not when it links the channel, not on a later save, and not when someone joins the project. If no channel has the name, the write is refused. A private channel counts as missing until the Flightdeck app is a member, so **for a private channel, invite the Flightdeck app to it in Slack first**.

Either refusal is the HTTP 422 `slack_channel_unusable` described above: nothing is saved, and the apply fails with Flightdeck's message on this attribute (a warning instead on the apply that creates the project). Applying the same configuration again gets the same answer, so change `mode` or `name` first. On a channel that is enabled but not linked yet, changing the mode runs the check again under the new mode.

Switching a linked channel to `create` makes Flightdeck check whether it made that channel. While the channel is enabled and Slack answers, that check happens during the write, and the write is refused if Flightdeck did not make it. When the channel is turned off, or Slack cannot be reached, Flightdeck saves the switch, keeps the link and invites nobody into it. Its background job checks the channel later (for a channel that is off, once it is turned on again), and if Flightdeck did not make the channel, `provision_status` then reads `failed` and `provision_note` says why. Switching never undoes anything: members already invited stay in the channel, and a linked channel stays linked.

A project where nobody has chosen reads null, and Flightdeck keeps the behavior from before the mode existed: it links a channel with that name if there is one, creates it if not, and invites the members either way. When unset, the project's current mode is kept and nothing is sent, so removing the attribute plans no change. Flightdeck has no way to go back to null once a mode is set.

Needs the Flightdeck release that added the Slack channel mode. On an older Flightdeck it reads as null; leave it unset there, because Flightdeck refuses it and the provider asks you to upgrade Flightdeck (an error, or a warning on the apply that creates the project).
- `name` (String) Channel name to use instead of the project-name default, stored as you write it (Flightdeck only trims surrounding whitespace, which is why that whitespace is not a diff). The Slack-legal name derived from it — lower case, runs of other characters collapsed to `-`, at most 80 characters — is reported as `basename`, so `Release Eng` here means channel `release-eng`. A name with no letter or digit is refused, since it would derive to nothing. When unset the project's current value is kept, so **set it to `""` to clear an override** and fall back to the project-name default — removing the attribute leaves whatever is there. Changing the derived name drops the stored `channel_id` so the next provision links the new channel; the old one is left on Slack.
- `notifications_enabled` (Boolean) Master switch for this project's Slack posts (the `slack` key of the project's `features`). When false, every project-scoped Slack post is silenced, even with a workspace default channel; channel provisioning is independent of it. When unset, the project's current value is kept. This is the only place the API accepts the `slack` feature — writing it in `features` is refused.

Read-Only:

- `available` (Boolean) Whether the workspace has a connected Slack integration. False means nothing will provision.
- `basename` (String) The effective channel name the provisioner uses: `name` normalized, or the project-name default.
- `channel_id` (String) Slack's id for the linked channel, set by the provision job. Null until it lands.
- `invites_skipped` (Number) Project members the latest invite cycle could not invite (no Slack match, or the connection cannot read e-mail addresses). Non-zero means linked, but not everyone is in.
- `linked` (Boolean) Whether a Slack channel is linked to this project (`channel_id` is set).
- `provision_note` (String) Short note from the provision job, such as the channel it created or why it failed.
- `provision_status` (String) Outcome of the asynchronous provision: `queued`, `provisioning`, `linked`, `needs_invite` or `failed`. `needs_invite` means the channel is linked, but Flightdeck is not in it and cannot join it by itself (a private channel it was removed from, an archived one, or a connection without permission to join), so it cannot invite members until someone adds the Flightdeck app to the channel; `provision_note` says what to do. Null when nothing has been enqueued.
- `scopes_sufficient` (Boolean) Whether the workspace's Slack connection has the channel scopes. False means provisioning will fail until an admin re-authorizes Slack.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by numeric id ...
terraform import flightdeck_project.app 42

# ... or by project identifier.
terraform import flightdeck_project.app APP
```
